# Fleet Deployments with Colmena and Deploy-RS

Iterating with `nixos-rebuild --target-host` one server at a time fails when managing tens or hundreds of nodes across multiple data centers. The boring default is: **orchestrating parallel, tag-targeted, zero-downtime fleet deployments with Colmena, complete with automated canary node validation and rollback guarantees**.

## Mental model

1. **Unified fleet hive:** A single Colmena hive definition (`hive.nix` or flake outputs) defines the configuration of all servers (gateways, application nodes, databases) in your organization.
2. **Parallel local evaluation:** Colmena evaluates all node configurations concurrently on your workstation or CI builder, builds their closures, and pushes them to target nodes over SSH in parallel.
3. **Atomic activation with auto-rollback:**
   - Colmena activates the new generation on designated canary nodes first.
   - If health checks fail or SSH connectivity drops, Colmena immediately executes `--rollback` across the fleet, preventing widespread outages.

## Worked examples

### Case 1: Defining a multi-node fleet in `flake.nix`

Save as `flake.nix`:

```nix
# flake.nix
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-24.05";
    colmena.url = "github:zhaofengli/colmena";
  };

  outputs = { self, nixpkgs, colmena }: {
    colmena = {
      meta = {
        nixpkgs = import nixpkgs { system = "x86_64-linux"; };
      };

      # Edge Ingress Gateway
      "gw-01" = {
        deployment.targetHost = "203.0.113.10";
        deployment.tags = [ "gateway" "production" ];
        imports = [ ./hosts/gw-01.nix ];
      };

      # Application Node 01
      "app-01" = {
        deployment.targetHost = "203.0.113.11";
        deployment.tags = [ "app" "production" ];
        imports = [ ./hosts/app-01.nix ];
      };

      # Application Node 02
      "app-02" = {
        deployment.targetHost = "203.0.113.12";
        deployment.tags = [ "app" "production" ];
        imports = [ ./hosts/app-02.nix ];
      };
    };
  };
}
```

Applying changes across only application servers:

```bash
colmena apply --on @app
```

```
[INFO ] Enumerating nodes...
[INFO ] Selected 2 out of 3 nodes: app-01, app-02
[INFO ] Building closures in parallel...
[app-01] Built /nix/store/7q1a...-nixos-system-app-01-24.05
[app-02] Built /nix/store/8k2b...-nixos-system-app-02-24.05
[INFO ] Pushing closures via SSH...
[INFO ] Activating configurations...
[app-01] Success!
[app-02] Success!
[INFO ] Fleet deployment complete.
```

## The trap

The trap is **relying on target servers to evaluate and compile their own configurations**. If an unprivileged edge node runs out of RAM during `nix-eval`, the build OOMs and leaves the node unresponsive. Always build on a dedicated CI builder or deployment machine and push pre-compiled closures.

## The boring rule

- Define all fleet hosts inside a unified Colmena flake output.
- Target subgroups using declarative tags (`@gateway`, `@app`, `@database`).
- Use `--keep-result` and automated rollbacks on canary nodes during automated rollouts.

## Try this

1. Run `colmena eval` against a two-node hive to test configuration syntax without connecting to nodes.
2. Check deployment graph dependencies with `colmena exec uname -a`.
